minutes.headline: Sewer Commission subcommittee reviewed Leominster's 25-year IMA renewal proposal and agreed to send back redlines, no vote on terms.
minutes.summary: The subcommittee went through Leominster's redlined proposal for renewing the intermunicipal sewer agreement for another 25 years. They discussed flow capacity, connection fees, user rates, emergency assistance and term length, and agreed on points to send back to Leominster. The only vote was adjournment.

budget_items.topic: User fee / rate per unit to Leominster
budget_items.what_was_said: Rate increase discussed as hard to negotiate; Lunenburg users should pay the same as Leominster residents.
Leominster approved the existing daily flow and will consider additional flows at its discretion; current use is around three hundred thousand. Option to increase to a higher figure was raised.
Leominster proposes a higher connection fee than the current average; the group wants to redline it and ask what Leominster residents pay.

budget_items.topic: Multi-family connection fee example and removed discount
budget_items.what_was_said: Multi-family units would pay the per-unit fee for each unit; a prior discount appears removed and the group will ask why.

budget_items.topic: New fee chart and usage rate (section 17)
budget_items.what_was_said: Per-unit usage rate rises under the new chart; commercial and school connection charges looked high and may be redlined. Lunenburg increases are tied to Leominster's single-family rate.
Reimbursement for the flood-related extra flows has been requested but will take a long time.

budget_items.topic: Inflow and infiltration reduction / sewer covers
budget_items.what_was_said: The Select Board gave funding for sewer covers and more is being sought at town meeting.

decisions.decision: Summary of points to send back to Leominster: flow request language, connection fees redline, new fee chart and user fee increase, fiscal-to-calendar-year change acceptable.
Add a request that Leominster provide manpower and equipment for major blockages and backups, and soften the 90-day termination and immediate stop-of-service remedies.
Ask Leominster about increasing Lunenburg's flow capacity now and keep the term at 25 years.

what_happened.line: A Sewer Commission subcommittee reviewed Leominster's redlined proposal to renew the intermunicipal sewer agreement for 25 years and took no vote on terms.
The group agreed on points to send back to Leominster: flow request language, a redline of connection fees, the new fee chart and user fee increase, and a fiscal-to-calendar-year change.
The group agreed to ask Leominster for manpower and equipment during major blockages and backups, and to soften the 90-day termination and immediate stop-of-service remedies.
The group agreed to ask Leominster about raising Lunenburg's flow capacity now while keeping the term at 25 years.
The only vote was to adjourn.

why_it_matters: The renewal sets the connection fees and per-unit user rates that Lunenburg sewer users pay Leominster, so the final terms feed into sewer bills and what new connections cost.
The agreement would run 25 years and decides how much flow Lunenburg may send to Leominster, which limits how much sewered development the town can add.
